items.title: Section: The Self-and-Other-Benefit Chapter Closes — What Actually Makes Benefit Final Rather Than Temporary

items.zh: 謂於欲界財寶具足、自體具足若因若果，及諸異生世間清淨若因若果，是不畢竟自利利他。若諸煩惱一切永斷，若諸所有八支聖道，若此為依獲得一切世間善法，是名畢竟自利利他。
items.en: Wealth and bodily endowment within the desire realm, whether as cause or fruit, and the mundane purification of an ordinary being, whether as cause or fruit — these are not genuinely final self-and-other-benefit … the complete and permanent severance of every affliction, the noble eightfold path itself, and every mundane wholesome quality resting upon that path — this is called genuinely final self-and-other-benefit.

items.zh: 由三因緣，應知畢竟及不畢竟。一、由自性故；二、由退不退故；三、由受用果有盡無盡故。由自性故者，究竟涅槃，名為畢竟；一切有為，名不畢竟。由退不退及受用果有盡無盡故者，八支聖道無有退故，及受用果無有盡故，名為畢竟；其餘一切善有漏法，由有退故，及受用果有終盡故，名不畢竟。
items.en: By three causes and conditions, one should know what is genuinely final and what is not: first, by its own nature; second, by whether it can regress or not; third, by whether its enjoyed fruit is exhaustible or not … ultimate nirvāṇa is called genuinely final; every conditioned thing is called not genuinely final … the noble eightfold path never regresses, and its enjoyed fruit is inexhaustible, so it is called genuinely final; every other wholesome but contaminated quality can regress, and its enjoyed fruit eventually runs out, so it is called not genuinely final.

items.zh: 如是菩薩十種自利利他，若略若廣，菩薩隨力隨能當勤修學。除此無有若過若增。過去未來所有一切已學當學自利利他，亦皆唯有如此十種自利利他。除此無有若過若增。

items.title: Section: The Chapter on True Meaning Opens — Two Kinds of Truth Beneath Everything

items.zh: 云何真實義？謂略有二種。一者、依如所有性，諸法真實性，二者、依盡所有性，諸法一切性。如是諸法真實性、一切性，應知總名真實義。此
items.en: What is true meaning? In brief, there are two kinds: first, resting on suchness itself, the true nature of all phenomena; second, resting on exhaustive content, the entirety of all phenomena. This true nature and this entirety together are called, in sum, true meaning.

items.title: Section: Seven Kinds of Suchness — Reading Reality's Unchanging Nature Through the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 真實義品類差別，復有四種。一者、世間極成真實，二者、道理極成真實，三者、煩惱障淨智所行真實，四者、所知障淨智所行真實。云何世間極成真實？謂一切世間，於彼彼事隨順假立、世俗串習、悟入覺慧所見同性。
items.en: The suchness of flux: that all conditioned processes have no fixed prior-or-later nature. The suchness of characteristics: the selflessness of the person and the selflessness of phenomena in every dharma. The suchness of cognition: that all conditioned processes are nothing but consciousness itself. The suchness of what is established: what I have taught as the noble truth of suffering. The suchness of erring conduct: what I have taught as the noble truth of origin. The suchness of purification: what I have taught as the noble truth of cessation. The suchness of right conduct: what I have taught as the noble truth of the path.

items.title: Four Depths of Truth: What the World Agrees On, and What Reason Actually Proves

items.zh: 謂地唯是地，非是火等。如地如是，水、火、風、色、聲、香、味、觸，飲食衣乘諸莊嚴具、資產什物，塗香、華鬘、歌舞伎樂、種種光明、男女承事、田園、邸店、宅舍等事，當知亦爾。苦唯是苦，非是樂等；樂唯是樂，非是苦等。以要言之，此即如此，非不如此；是即如是，非不如是。決定勝解所行境事，一切世間從其本際展轉傳來，想自分別共所成立，不由思惟、籌量、觀察，然後方取。是名世間極成真實。
items.en: Earth is simply earth, not fire, and so on … in short: this is simply this, not otherwise; that is simply that, not otherwise — the object of a firm, settled conviction, handed down since beginningless time throughout the world, established jointly through ordinary conceptual habit, grasped without any prior deliberation, weighing, or examination. This is called world-established truth.

items.zh: 謂諸智者有道理義。諸聰叡者、諸黠慧者、能尋思者、能伺察者、住尋伺地者、具自辯才者、居異生位者、隨觀察行者，依止現、比及至教量，極善思擇決定智所行、所知事，由證成道理所建立、所施設義。是名道理極成真實。云何煩惱障淨智所行真實？
items.en: The wise possess reasoned understanding … resting on direct perception, inference, and scriptural authority, they most excellently investigate and settle the object of understanding through the principle of valid demonstration, establishing and articulating its meaning. This is called reason-established truth.

items.title: Section: The Hearer's Purified Truth — Direct Realisation of No-Self Through the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 謂一切聲聞、獨覺，若無漏智、若能引無漏智、若無漏後得世間智所行境界，是名煩惱障淨智所行真實。由緣此為境，從煩惱障智得清淨，於當來世無障礙住，是故說名煩惱障淨智所行真實。
items.en: The object experienced by every hearer's and solitary buddha's uncontaminated wisdom, the wisdom that leads towards it, and the uncontaminated wisdom attained afterwards — this is called the truth belonging to purification from the afflictive obstruction. By taking this as their object, they become purified from the afflictive obstruction, and abide without obstruction in every future life — for this reason, it is called the truth belonging to purification from the afflictive obstruction.

items.zh: 此復云何？謂四聖諦。一、苦聖諦，二、集聖諦，三、滅聖諦，四、道聖諦。即於如是四聖諦義極善思擇，證入現觀。入現觀已，如實智生。此諦現觀，聲聞、獨覺能觀唯有諸蘊可得，除諸蘊外我不可得。數習緣生諸行生滅相應慧故，數習異蘊補特伽羅無性見故，發生如是聖諦現觀。
items.en: Through direct realisation of this truth, hearers and solitary buddhas are able to observe that only the aggregates are to be found, with no self to be found apart from them. Through repeated cultivation of the wisdom that corresponds to conditioned processes' own arising and ceasing, and through repeated cultivation of the insight that no self exists distinct from the aggregates, this direct realisation of the noble truths comes about.

items.zh: 云何所知障淨智所行真實？

items.title: Section: The Bodhisattva's Purified Truth — Realising That Phenomena Themselves Have No Fixed Nature

items.zh: 謂於所知能礙智故，名所知障。從所知障得解脫智所行境界，當知是名所知障淨智所行真實。
items.en: Whatever obstructs wisdom with respect to what is known is called the cognitive obstruction. The object experienced by the wisdom that has become liberated from this cognitive obstruction should be known as the truth belonging to purification from the cognitive obstruction.

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩諸佛世尊入法無我，入已善淨，於一切法離言自性、假說自性平等平等無分別智所行境界。
items.en: Bodhisattvas and buddhas enter into the selflessness of phenomena, and, having entered, become thoroughly purified — this is the object of the non-discriminating wisdom that, regarding every phenomenon's inexpressible nature and its merely designated nature, rests in utter equality, free both of taking the former as nonexistent and of taking the latter as truly existent.

blocks.text: The chapter on self-benefit closes, and the **chapter on true meaning** (真實義品) opens. This chapter is the philosophical heart of the Bodhisattva Stage: a sustained argument about what is real, and how language relates to it. A short passage (0486a09) is untranslated.

Wealth, bodily endowment, and worldly purification "are not genuinely final". "The complete and permanent severance of every affliction" and the noble path are final. Three tests: by nature; by whether it can regress; by whether its fruit is exhaustible. "Ultimate nirvāṇa is final; every conditioned thing is not."
"Two kinds: resting on suchness, the true nature of all phenomena; and resting on exhaustive content, the entirety of all phenomena." Master Cháng Bǎi: 真 (true) rules out the erroneous.

items: **Truth established by the world**: "Earth is simply earth, not fire"; "handed down since beginningless time, established by ordinary conceptual habit", "grasped without deliberation".
**Truth established by reasoning**: what the wise "investigate and settle through direct perception, inference, and scripture".

**The truth known by wisdom purified of the afflictive obstruction**: the object of hearers' and solitary buddhas' uncontaminated wisdom, through which they see that "only the aggregates are found, no self apart from them".

**The truth known by wisdom purified of the cognitive obstruction**: "Bodhisattvas and Buddhas enter the selflessness of phenomena", the object of "non-discriminating wisdom" regarding "every phenomenon's inexpressible nature".

blocks.text: The four are a ladder: common sense, reasoned knowledge, the hearer's insight into no-self of persons, and the bodhisattva's insight into no-self of phenomena. Each is "true" at its level.

quiz.q: "An ordinary being's mundane purification is not final benefit." Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: with dhyāna, afflictions don't arise — but seeds remain; it's still contaminated
quiz.why: "And the mundane purification of an ordinary being, whether as cause or fruit — these are not genuinely final self-and-other-benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: with dhyāna, afflictions don't arise — but that doesn't mean there are none; their seeds aren't cut, so it's still contaminated.

quiz.q: "Every other wholesome contaminated quality is not final." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish ordinary and noble merit?
options: ordinary merit is contaminated, noble merit uncontaminated
quiz.why: "Every other wholesome but contaminated quality can regress, and its enjoyed fruit eventually runs out, so it is called not genuinely final." Venerable Miào Jìng: ordinary beings' merit is contaminated; the noble ones' is uncontaminated — they differ.

quiz.q: "What is true meaning (真實義)?" How does Master Cháng Bǎi break down the three characters?
options: 真 rules out error, 實 distinguishes from falsehood, 義 is the object
quiz.why: "What is true meaning? In brief, there are two kinds." Master Cháng Bǎi: 真 rules out the erroneous; 實 distinguishes from the false; 義 is the object.

quiz.q: "Suchness itself" and "exhaustive content" — how do the masters explain?
options: Cháng Bǎi, after Tàixū: principled wisdom knows suchness, quantifying wisdom exhaustive content; Miào Jìng: 盡 means including all things without remainder
quiz.why: "First, resting on suchness itself, the true nature of all phenomena; second, resting on exhaustive content, the entirety of all phenomena." Master Cháng Bǎi: Tàixū says principled wisdom penetrates suchness, and quantifying wisdom penetrates exhaustive content. Venerable Miào Jìng: 盡 includes all things — nothing left out.

quiz.q: World-established truth is "grasped without deliberation, weighing, or examination." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: "this is called snow" — no need to ask why
quiz.why: "Grasped without any prior deliberation, weighing, or examination." Venerable Miào Jìng: "this is called snow" — don't ask why it's called snow; no need!

quiz.q: Reason-established truth rests on "direct perception, inference, and scripture." How does Venerable Miào Jìng illustrate inference?
options: seeing smoke, one knows there's fire
quiz.why: "Resting on direct perception, inference, and scriptural authority, they most excellently investigate and settle the object of understanding." Venerable Miào Jìng: because one sees smoke, one knows there's fire.

quiz.q: "What obstructs wisdom regarding the knowable is the cognitive obstruction." What ignorance is it, per the masters?
options: ignorance as clinging to phenomena — subtle clinging to all things
quiz.why: "Whatever obstructs wisdom with respect to what is known is called the cognitive obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: what is this ignorance? Clinging to phenomena — subtle clinging towards all things. Master Cháng Bǎi: the cognitive obstruction means the ignorance of clinging to phenomena.
